newsitem.title: DUBAI: Horse racing-Singspiel wins world's richest race.
newsitem.headline: Horse racing-Singspiel wins world's richest race.

text.p: Singspiel, trained in England by Michael Stoute and ridden by American Jerry Bailey, won the Dubai World Cup horse race, the world's richest, on Thursday.
Second place went to Siphon, the mount of David Flores, with Sandpit, ridden by Corey Nakatani, in third.
Betting is not allowed in Dubai, but the winner had been quoted in London betting offices at 13-2.
The race, worth 1.4 million pounds ($2.3 million) to the winner, was due to have been run last Saturday, but had to be postponed because of torrential downpour.
Bailey won the inaugural running of the World Cup in 1996 on Cigar, while Singspiel took last year's Japan Cup, when ridden by Frankie Dettori.
Two horses fell in Thursday's race, English-trained Bijou d'Inde appearing to bring down Japan's Hokuto Vega towards the rear of the field with about 600 metres left.
